cards.text: Paul, called to be an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the believers in Rome (Romans 1:1, 7). He just said God did not reject His people Israel (Romans 11:2), a remnant was chosen by grace (Romans 11:5), and the others were hardened (Romans 11:7). Now Paul asks the big one: did they stumble so as to fall beyond recovery?

cards.question: Paul says Israel stumbled so badly that they fell beyond recovery.

cards.text: Paul's answer: “Certainly not!” ZERO wiggle room, friend. But because of Israel's trespass, something has come to the Gentiles.

cards.question: Because of Israel's trespass, what has come to the Gentiles?

cards.text: And Paul says why: salvation has come to the Gentiles to make Israel jealous.
Watch Paul now, baker. This man is about to do MATH: if Israel's trespass means riches for the world, and their failure means riches for the Gentiles, then what?

cards.question: What does Paul say Israel's fullness will bring?

cards.text: Then Paul talks straight to the Gentiles. He's the apostle to the Gentiles, and he magnifies his ministry, hoping to provoke his own people to jealousy.

cards.question: Paul hopes to provoke his own people to jealousy and ___ some of them.

cards.text: And Paul will NOT sit down. If their rejection is the reconciliation of the world, he asks, what will their acceptance be?

cards.question: Paul asks what Israel's acceptance will be. What does he call it?

cards.text: Then Paul pulls out a picture, and baker, it's DOUGH. Say that word around a cookie stamper and watch my mustache stand straight up.

cards.question: Paul says the first part of the dough is holy. What does he say about the whole batch?

answers.text: The whole batch is holy too
Only that first part is holy
The rest must be made holy

cards.question: Right after the dough, Paul gives a tree picture: if the root is holy, so are the branches.

cards.text: Paul stays with that tree, still talking to the Gentiles. If some branches have been broken off, he says, and you, a wild olive shoot, have been grafted in among the others to share in the nourishment of the olive root, then listen up.

cards.question: What does Paul tell the wild olive shoot not to do over the broken-off branches?
Paul reminds the grafted-in wild shoot that the root supports it.

cards.text: Paul sees the comeback coming from the wild shoot: “Branches were broken off so that I could be grafted in.” Paul agrees that's correct, and friend, when somebody agrees with you and KEEPS talking, brace yourself.
Here's where Paul keeps talking: those natural branches were broken off because of unbelief.

cards.question: The natural branches were broken off because of unbelief, but Paul says the grafted-in shoot stands by ___.

cards.text: Then Paul says, “Do not be arrogant, but be afraid.” And he gives a reason.

cards.question: Paul says that if God did not spare the natural branches, He will surely spare the grafted-in ones.

cards.text: So Paul says take notice. He wants the Gentiles looking at two things about God, not just one.

cards.question: Branches broken off, a wild shoot grafted in. Which two things about God does Paul tell the Gentiles to notice?
Paul says God shows severity to those who fell. What condition does he give the grafted-in Gentiles?

cards.text: Then Paul adds a warning, and he doesn't soften it one bit: “Otherwise you also will be cut off.”
Now Paul turns back to the branches that got broken off. Lean in for this part, baker.

cards.question: Paul says that if the broken-off branches do not persist in unbelief, they will be grafted in.

cards.text: Paul gives the reason: God is able to graft them in again. Then his last move: if the Gentiles were cut from a wild olive tree and grafted into a cultivated one, contrary to nature, think about the branches that grew there first.

cards.question: If a wild shoot was grafted into a cultivated olive tree, contrary to nature, what does Paul say about the natural branches?

answers.text: They'll be grafted in more readily
They'll be grafted in more slowly
They'll need a different olive tree
